segments.text: State management often boils down to one tricky problem
how do you update specific parts of your UI
when your data changes without rebuilding your whole app.
Imagine a chaotic version of the classic counter app
where the count appears everywhere,
ignoring how unconventional this UI is.
You still need to update all these widgets
when the count changes.
A great solution for this is the change notifier class.
Change notifier is a class that notifies subscribed widgets when
it's time to rebuild.
To use it, create a class that extends change notifier.
Add properties that expose the state the changes
and methods that know how to update that state.
Then in those methods, call the notify listeners method
after the state has changed.
This is the signal that will cause listening widgets
to rebuild.
To listen in your UI.
Use a listenable builder.
This widget takes a listenable like our counter model
and a builder function.
Now whenever notify listeners is called,
each subscribed listenable builder
reruns its builder method to rebuild their widget,
and your UI stays perfectly in sync.
For more info on change notifier and other Flutter techniques,
head to flutter.dev.
